page: Microsoft Azure E64ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Eadv6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and features 512.0 GB of RAM, translating to a resource density of 8.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled with a 3780 GB local disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates strong overall performance, with Geekbench multi-core scores and image processing capabilities reaching the top 10% tier. Stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance, along with Passmark CPU and memory scores, consistently rank in the top 25%. In memory operations, the server exhibits strong write bandwidth for large blocks and small-block read-only cached bandwidth, though large-block read-only uncached bandwidth falls into the middle 50% average. For specialized workloads, the instance demonstrates top-tier prompt processing speeds for small language models, while text generation and medium-model inference remain strong.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E64ads_v6 offers high memory density and substantial local storage capacity, reducing the need for external storage attachments for data-intensive operations. However, the lack of a dedicated GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, and large-block uncached memory reads represent a minor performance tradeoff compared to its cached memory speeds. This hardware profile is suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, software compilation, and large-scale web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure E64ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Eadv6 family, featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor at 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM and 3780 GB of local storage. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the server demonstrates strong benchmark performance, with Geekbench multi-core and image processing scores reaching the top 10% tier. While large-block uncached memory reads perform at an average level, the instance excels in multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and small-model LLM prompt processing. This configuration provides a high-density memory-to-CPU ratio without a GPU, making it highly efficient for database hosting, memory-intensive enterprise applications, and software compilation.
